name: Tick-Level Trade Execution Matching via Native ASOF JOIN
description: In algorithmic trading, every buy or sell order must be evaluated against the most recent prevailing market quote. Standard relational equality joins fail because quotes and trades happen at irregular microsecond intervals.
expected_columns: trade_id; symbol; trade_time; executed_price; shares; prevailing_quote_time; bid_price; ask_price; slippage
why_it_fails: LLMs typically write quadratic triangular self-joins (WHERE q.ts <= t.ts) or window functions with LAG/LAST_VALUE, which create massive memory spikes on high-frequency streams.

name: Multi-Currency Point-in-Time FX Conversion via ASOF JOIN
description: Global payments systems record transactions in local currencies (EUR, JPY, GBP) that must be converted to USD using the prevailing exchange rate at the exact transaction millisecond.
expected_columns: payment_id; payment_time; currency; amount_local; rate_to_usd; amount_usd; fx_snapshot_time
why_it_fails: Joining to a daily FX table using DATE(ts) loses intraday volatility and causes currency conversion discrepancies of up to 1-2% during volatile market events.

name: Clickstream Sessionization with Inactivity Timeouts (Gaps & Islands)
description: Digital analytics platforms group raw user pageviews into 'sessions'. If a user is inactive for more than 30 minutes, the next click begins a brand-new session.
why_it_fails: Models mistakenly partition by user_id and take ROW_NUMBER(), which fails to segment sessions by time gaps, or use self-joins which scale quadratically.

name: Sliding Sessionization with Absolute Maximum Duration Cap
description: Real-world web sessions often need dual constraints: a 30-minute inactivity timeout AND a strict maximum 4-hour absolute session duration to prevent bots from maintaining endless sessions.
why_it_fails: A simple inactivity check keeps sessions alive indefinitely if events happen every 10 minutes. Tracking session origin requires window frames with state.

name: IoT Sensor Telemetry Gap-Filling via generate_series and LOCF
description: Industrial IoT sensors emit readings intermittently to save bandwidth. Downstream machine learning models require strict continuous 1-minute time grids with Last Observation Carried Forward (LOCF).
why_it_fails: Using OUTER JOIN without dynamic range generation leaves temporal voids, leading to missing periods in downstream feature stores.

name: Bitemporal Auditing: Valid-Time vs. Transaction-Time Alignment
description: Financial compliance requires knowing: 'What did we believe customer Alice's credit limit was on May 15th, based on what was entered into our database as of June 1st?' (Bitemporal query).
expected_columns: customer_id; limit_as_known_then; valid_from; valid_to; system_from; system_to
why_it_fails: Relying on a single timestamp column confuses retroactive corrections with real-world effective dates, causing compliance audit failures.

name: Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 Join with Open-Ended Future
description: Customers change addresses or account tiers over time. Joining historical orders to customer profile dimensions requires matching the order date to the active validity interval.
why_it_fails: Current active records typically have `valid_to IS NULL`. A simple `order_date BETWEEN valid_from AND valid_to` drops all current active records.

name: Hopping / Overlapping Window Aggregations via time_bucket
description: Real-time surveillance monitors rolling 15-minute average latency stepped forward every 5 minutes (a hopping window).
expected_columns: window_start; window_end; server_id; sample_count; avg_cpu; peak_cpu
why_it_fails: Standard GROUP BY time_bucket only produces non-overlapping tumbling windows, missing cross-boundary bursts.

name: Financial Ledger Cumulative Balance with Duplicate Timestamp Ties
description: Ledger entries can occur at the exact same millisecond. Financial ledgers must preserve strict incremental balances rather than bunching peer rows.
why_it_fails: SQL window functions default to `RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`, which aggregates identical timestamps together into the same running total.

name: Window Frame Exclusion: Peer Period Average via EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW
description: To detect anomalous spikes, analysts compare a metric against the average of neighboring days, strictly excluding the current day's value to avoid skewing the baseline.
why_it_fails: Computing rolling averages without excluding the current row inflates the baseline during the spike itself, hiding the anomaly.

name: Excluding Ties in Percentile Ranks via EXCLUDE TIES
description: When evaluating employee sales performance, ties should not inflate the percentile score against colleagues who achieved the exact same result.
why_it_fails: Using standard RANK() causes tied individuals to push each other's percentiles higher or lower inconsistently.

name: Inter-Packet Network Arrival Jitter at Nanosecond Resolution
description: High-speed network telemetry measures packet arrival jitter (variance in inter-packet delay). Jitter spikes indicate network congestion or buffer bloat.
why_it_fails: Standard SQL datetime arithmetic truncates to milliseconds or seconds, losing high-frequency microsecond microbursts.

name: Point-in-Time Limit Order Book (LOB) State Reconstruction
description: Market microstructure researchers need to reconstruct the exact bids and asks available at an arbitrary point in time from an append-only event stream of place, cancel, and fill orders.
why_it_fails: Summing active orders without filtering out cancellations that occurred before the target time produces a phantom order book.

name: Time-Weighted Average Price (TWAP) with Variable Interval Weights
description: TWAP measures the average price of an asset weighted by the duration of time that each price level was sustained, preventing brief price spikes from distorting valuation.
why_it_fails: Taking simple AVG(price) biases the result towards periods with frequent tick updates rather than sustained duration.

name: Intraday Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP) Resetting Daily
description: VWAP provides institutional traders the definitive benchmark price weighted by traded volume, resetting to zero at the start of every trading day.
why_it_fails: Failing to partition by trading date mixes multi-day volume into the intraday numerator and denominator.

name: Chronological Multi-Stage Conversion Funnel with Time Boundaries
description: In product funnels (Signup -> Verify -> Purchase), events must occur in exact chronological order, with each step completed within 24 hours of the previous.
why_it_fails: Models join events without checking timestamp ordering (e.g., verifying after purchase), artificially inflating funnel conversion.

name: Dynamic User Retention Cohort Matrix by Weekly Milestones
description: SaaS analytics track weekly retention curves (Day 0, Day 7, Day 14, Day 30) based on user signup week.
why_it_fails: Calculating retention without dynamic date grouping produces rigid, fragile queries requiring manual updates every week.

name: Exponential Time-Decayed User Affinity Scoring
description: Recommendation systems score user interest where recent clicks count significantly more than clicks from 30 days ago, modeled via exponential decay: score * e^(-lambda * delta_days).
why_it_fails: Equal-weight counts overemphasize obsolete user interests from months ago.

name: Customer Churn Anomaly Detection vs Historical Purchase Rhythm
description: A customer who normally buys every 3 days is at risk if they haven't bought in 10 days. But a customer who buys quarterly is not. Churn detection must be personalized to each user's cadence.
why_it_fails: Static 30-day churn thresholds misflag seasonal or low-frequency high-value customers.

name: E-Commerce Financial Aggregation without Join Fan-Out
description: Demonstrates the Chasm Trap where joining multiple 1-to-many child tables (discounts and shipments) to an orders table causes row multiplication before aggregation, inflating financial sums.
why_it_fails: Joining multiple 1:N child tables (order_discounts has 2 rows, order_shipments has 2 rows) directly to orders before GROUP BY creates an intermediate Cartesian fan-out of 2 * 2 = 4 rows per order. Aggregating over these inflated rows multiplies base_amount by 4x ($100.00 -> $400.00), total discounts by 2x ($15.00 -> $30.00), and shipping by 2x ($10.00 -> $20.00). Proper solution requires pre-aggregating child tables to 1 row per order in CTEs or correlated subqueries before joining.

name: Peak Concurrent Workforce Capacity via Interval Overlap Scan
description: Workforce managers must calculate maximum concurrent staffing levels from employee shift start and end times to ensure warehouse safety limits are never breached.
why_it_fails: Pairwise self-joins between overlapping shifts blow up to O(N^2) complexity.

name: Continuous Asset Lease Unallocated Gap Discovery
description: Fleet managers track commercial vehicles to find idle 'unrented' gaps between back-to-back rental contracts for fleet utilization auditing.
why_it_fails: Comparing each row with LEAD without filtering where next_start > current_end misses adjacent non-overlapping bookings.

name: Bi-directional Linear Value Interpolation between Observations
description: When a sensor drops offline for 30 minutes, data scientists prefer linear interpolation between the last known reading and the next recovered reading rather than flat zero-filling.
why_it_fails: Requires simultaneous look-behind (LAG) and look-ahead (LEAD) across varying time distances.

name: Outlier-Resistant Rolling Window (Trimmed Mean Aggregation)
description: Financial risk models compute a 7-day rolling average excluding the highest and lowest single observations in each 7-day window to eliminate transient flash crashes.
why_it_fails: Writing self-joins with sub-aggregations to filter min/max results in huge query execution trees.

name: SARGable Fiscal Year Date Range Partition Pruning
description: Data warehouses partition petabyte event tables by date. Wrapping date columns in functions (e.g. `WHERE strftime('%Y', event_time) = '2026'`) breaks partition pruning, forcing a full table scan.
why_it_fails: Non-SARGable functions force DuckDB/Snowflake to scan every Parquet row group.

name: Multi-Touch Marketing Attribution Comparison in a Single Pass
description: CMOs need to compare 3 attribution models (First-Touch, Last-Touch, and Uniform Linear) for touchpoints occurring within 30 days prior to conversion.
why_it_fails: Running three separate join queries triples warehouse compute costs and risks data inconsistency.

name: Dense Vector Cosine Similarity Nearest Neighbors (Top-K ANN)
description: When a user asks a question in an AI assistant, the query is embedded into a dense vector (e.g. 4-dimensional here for illustration, or 384/1536 in prod). We retrieve the top most semantically relevant documentation chunks.
why_it_fails: Models frequently try to calculate cosine similarity manually using dot product divided by norms in SQL, which is slow, verbose, and numerically unstable with zero vectors.

name: L2 Euclidean Distance Nearest Neighbors Search via array_distance
description: In computer vision feature retrieval (facial recognition, product image matching), feature vectors are compared using Euclidean (L2) distance where lower distance equals higher visual similarity.
why_it_fails: LLMs often try to write SQRT(SUM(POW(a - b, 2))) which prevents vectorized hardware acceleration.

name: Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) for Normalized Embeddings
description: For unit-normalized vectors (e.g. OpenAI text-embedding-3 or Cohere embeddings), cosine similarity is identical to the inner product (dot product), which executes even faster.
why_it_fails: Re-normalizing vectors in every query wastes compute when embeddings are pre-normalized upon insertion.

name: The Pre-Filtering Trap: Relational Predicates with Vector Top-K
description: A user searches for 'cheap mechanical keyboard under $50'. If you run vector search Top-K first and filter by price afterwards (post-filtering), you may return zero products because all top-5 matches were $150 keyboards.
why_it_fails: Post-filtering vector results breaks recall. Relational constraints (in-stock, price bounds, user tenant_id) must be evaluated as PRE-FILTERS before Top-K ranking.

name: Clickstream Sessionization with Inactivity Gaps
description: Groups web analytics events into browsing sessions where an inactivity gap greater than 30 minutes demarcates a new session boundary.
why_it_fails: Sessionization with inactivity timeouts is a classic Gaps & Islands problem. Naive LLMs routinely attempt to group directly by timestamps or confuse ROW_NUMBER() with session grouping, failing to calculate the cumulative sum of step flags (LAG condition). The optimal pattern requires a two-step window CTE: step 1 identifies boundary leaps (> 30 min) with LAG(), and step 2 computes a running cumulative sum of those flags to assign unique session IDs.

name: Adaptive Similarity Thresholding with Fallback Top-K Guarantee
description: RAG systems want high-confidence matches (similarity > 0.85) to avoid hallucinations, but if no document exceeds 0.85, they need a guaranteed top-1 fallback to provide at least some context.
why_it_fails: A hard WHERE similarity > 0.85 yields empty sets, while a raw LIMIT 5 includes irrelevant noise.

name: Semantic Deduplication of IT Incident Tickets via Vector Cosine Threshold
description: During service outages, hundreds of users submit identically phrased IT support tickets ('login down', 'cannot access account'). Clustering tickets with vector similarity > 0.88 consolidates duplicates into a single incident.
why_it_fails: Quadratic N x N self-joins without ordering check (`t1.id < t2.id`) double compute and compare tickets to themselves.

name: Multi-Merchant Near-Duplicate Catalog Resolution with Price Consistency
description: Marketplaces aggregate catalogs from thousands of sellers. Matching identical items requires high semantic vector similarity AND compatible price bounds (e.g. price within 20%).
expected_columns: sku_a; merchant_a; title_a; sku_b; merchant_b; title_b; similarity; price_difference_pct
why_it_fails: Vector similarity alone matches accessories to main products; price filtering alone matches unrelated items.

name: ColBERT Multi-Vector Late Interaction (MaxSim) in Pure SQL
description: Advanced retrieval models (ColBERT / Sanity) represent queries and documents as collections of token vectors. Scoring computes MaxSim: for each query token, take the maximum cosine similarity across all document tokens, then sum.
why_it_fails: Implementing late interaction typically requires specialized Python tensor pipelines.

name: User Profile Preference Vector Centroid Aggregation
description: To personalize feeds, recommendation engines compute a dynamic user preference vector by calculating the average centroid of the embeddings of products the user clicked in the last 7 days.
why_it_fails: SQL standard lacks native array averaging; unnesting arrays without proper positional indexes scrambles vector dimensions.

name: K-Means Clustering Assignment and Centroid Update in Pure SQL
description: Unsupervised customer segmentation can be run directly inside DuckDB by assigning customer vectors to the nearest centroid and recomputing cluster means in a single query.
why_it_fails: Running ML clustering outside the warehouse requires exporting millions of vectors over the network.

name: Vector Anomaly Detection via Average K-Nearest Neighbor Distance
description: Anomalous sensor readings or fraudulent transaction vectors reside in sparse regions of the embedding space. Measuring the average distance to a vector's 3 nearest neighbors flags outliers.
why_it_fails: Setting a global static distance threshold fails when data clusters have variable local densities.

name: Cohort-Constrained Vector Match with Geographical Regionality
description: Real-world matchmaking (dating apps, gig-economy driver matching) requires vector personality/skill compatibility joined with strict relational geographic and category boundaries.
why_it_fails: Matching vectors globally without partitioning by region produces candidates located 3,000 miles away.

name: Multi-Modal Joint Retrieval (Image + Text Query Embedding Fusion)
description: In e-commerce search, users submit a photo and a text clarification (e.g. photo of dress + 'in floral silk'). We compute a weighted combination of image-vector and text-vector similarity.
why_it_fails: Treating text and image vectors as independent queries yields conflicting rank lists.

name: Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) Diversity Reranking in SQL
description: Standard vector retrieval often returns 5 virtually identical articles. MMR penalizes redundancy by selecting documents that are similar to the query but dissimilar to already-selected documents.
why_it_fails: Pure relevance search creates echo-chamber search results with zero content diversity.

name: Historical SCD Type 2 Point-in-Time Currency Conversion
description: Joins financial transactions to Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD Type 2) exchange rate tables matching effective date ranges, correctly handling open-ended NULL upper bounds.
why_it_fails: Frontier models routinely fail SCD Type 2 point-in-time join logic in two ways: (1) omitting the open-ended current record condition `OR valid_to IS NULL`, which causes current active records to be silently dropped during INNER JOINs, and (2) using `<=` instead of `<` on the upper boundary, which causes duplicate rows when a transaction occurs exactly on the boundary timestamp of an SCD revision.

name: Pairwise Vector Similarity Self-Join with Coarse Cluster Pruning
description: Finding all similar document pairs across 100,000 docs is O(N^2) (10 billion checks). Partitioning into coarse category buckets first reduces search to O(N * (N/K)).
why_it_fails: Unpartitioned cross joins cause out-of-memory crashes on analytical engines.

name: Latent Factor Matrix Factorization Dot Product Recommendation
description: Matrix factorization (SVD / ALS) maps users and movies to latent factor vectors. Predicted rating is dot product of user vector and movie vector plus user and movie bias terms.
why_it_fails: Omitting bias terms causes popular movies to be underrated and niche items to be overrated.

name: Vector Repulsion Scoring (Positive vs Negative Query Guidance)
description: In image generation and semantic search, users supply positive and negative prompts (e.g. 'cyberpunk city' NOT 'blurry / low quality'). The score boosts positive similarity and penalizes negative similarity.
why_it_fails: Filtering out negatives with boolean NOT drops items that have even slight overlap with negative words.

name: Document-Level Aggregation with Best-Chunk Pooling in RAG
description: Long PDF manuals are split into 50 chunks each. To avoid returning 5 chunks from the exact same PDF manual, we retrieve the best chunk per document and aggregate at the document level.
why_it_fails: Returning raw chunk Top-K dominates the context window with duplicates from a single document.

name: Dynamic Context Window Token Budget Packing for LLM RAG
description: When assembling retrieved chunks for an LLM prompt, you have a strict token limit (e.g. 1,000 tokens). You must greedily pick highest-similarity chunks until the cumulative token sum would exceed the budget.
why_it_fails: Picking a fixed LIMIT 10 can overflow LLM token limits or waste available prompt capacity.

name: Two-Stage Retrieval: Bi-Encoder Candidate Generation for Re-ranking
description: Modern enterprise search uses a 2-stage pipeline: Fast bi-encoder vector search retrieves Top-50 candidates, which are then passed to a computationally heavy cross-encoder for final scoring.
why_it_fails: Running heavy cross-encoder models across entire datasets is computationally impossible.

name: Temporal Semantic Drift Tracking across Document Embedding Centroids
description: As companies evolve, the meaning of terms like 'security' or 'remote work' shifts. Tracking the cosine distance between monthly embedding centroids reveals semantic concept drift.
why_it_fails: Ignoring semantic drift causes older documentation to silently diverge from current employee search queries.

name: Hierarchical Coarse-to-Fine Multi-Level Vector Filtering
description: In massive enterprise catalogs, searching 100 million items is accelerated by first matching high-level department embedding centroids, then searching specific item vectors inside matching departments.
why_it_fails: Flat brute-force vector search over hundreds of millions of items consumes excessive compute.

name: Vector Quantization Precision Distortion & Reconstruction Error
description: To compress embeddings from 32-bit floats to 8-bit integers, engineers evaluate the reconstruction error (distance between uncompressed and quantized vector) to measure fidelity loss.
why_it_fails: Deploying quantized embeddings without evaluating distortion leads to silent degradation in search accuracy.

name: Zero-Shot Query Intent Classification via Prototype Vector Distance
description: Instead of training a BERT classifier, user query vectors are compared against pre-computed 'intent prototype vectors' (e.g. Navigational, Transactional, Informational). The closest prototype labels the query intent.
why_it_fails: Maintaining external classifier microservices adds 50ms latency to query planning.

name: Customer Anti-Join with Three-Valued Null Semantics
description: Exposes silent data loss caused by SQL three-valued logic when models use NOT IN over subqueries containing NULLs.
why_it_fails: In ANSI SQL three-valued logic, `x NOT IN (1, NULL)` evaluates to `UNKNOWN` rather than TRUE because SQL cannot guarantee x is not equal to the unknown value. Consequently, any query using `WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM ...)` where the subquery contains even a single NULL value evaluates to UNKNOWN for all rows, silently returning 0 results. Correct solutions require NOT EXISTS or LEFT JOIN ... WHERE ... IS NULL.

name: Contrastive Triplet Evaluation: Anchor-Positive-Negative Separation
description: In embedding model evaluation, high-quality models satisfy the triplet condition: distance(anchor, positive) + margin < distance(anchor, negative). We evaluate model margin violations directly in SQL.
why_it_fails: Validating embedding models often requires ad-hoc PyTorch scripts; SQL evaluation enables continuous monitoring in production.

name: DuckDB Full-Text Search (FTS) BM25 Term Relevance Scoring
description: Traditional databases use simple `LIKE '%search%'` which treats 1 mention the same as 10 mentions and ignores document frequency. BM25 scores term saturation and document rarity.
why_it_fails: ILIKE matches substrings blindly (e.g. 'cat' matches 'scattered' or 'certificate') with zero relevancy ranking.

name: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) Hybrid Search (BM25 + Dense Vectors)
description: Hybrid search combines sparse keyword search (great for exact names and acronyms) with dense vector search (great for synonyms and concepts). RRF merges both rank lists using: RRF_score = 1/(60 + rank_bm25) + 1/(60 + rank_vec).
why_it_fails: Adding raw BM25 scores (range 0 to 50+) directly to cosine similarity scores (range 0 to 1) allows BM25 to completely drown out vector relevance.

name: Min-Max Normalized Convex Combination Hybrid Search
description: An alternative to rank-based RRF is score-based fusion: min-max scale lexical scores to [0, 1] and vector scores to [0, 1], then take alpha * lexical + (1 - alpha) * vector.
why_it_fails: Division by zero when all scores in a small result set are identical.

name: Typo-Tolerant Search with Levenshtein Edit Distance & Length Bounds
description: Users frequently misspell search terms (e.g. 'postgre' -> 'postgresql'). Levenshtein distance counts insertions, deletions, and substitutions.
why_it_fails: Computing Levenshtein distance on every catalog word is CPU intensive without pre-filtering on string length (ABS(len_a - len_b) <= max_distance).

name: Brand & Name Fuzzy Search via Jaro-Winkler Prefix Similarity
description: In e-commerce, users often mistype the suffixes of brand names ('Samsumg' vs 'Samsung'). Jaro-Winkler gives higher weight to prefix matches, making it ideal for proper names.
why_it_fails: Standard Levenshtein treats mistakes at the start of a word the same as at the end.

name: Multi-Field Weighted Full-Text Retrieval (Title 3x, Body 1x)
description: A match in a document title or product headline is far more indicative of relevance than a passing mention in the body text.
why_it_fails: Concatenating title and body into a single column gives equal weight to all words.

name: Exact Phrase Proximity Boosting in Keyword Retrieval
description: If a user searches for 'machine learning', an article containing the exact phrase 'machine learning' should rank higher than an article where 'machine' is in paragraph 1 and 'learning' is in paragraph 8.
why_it_fails: Pure bag-of-words keyword matches ignore token proximity and phrase boundaries.

name: Stopword Filtering and Query Token Cleansing in SQL
description: Search queries like 'what is the best laptop' contain stop words ('what', 'is', 'the') that dilute search precision if not filtered prior to catalog matching.
why_it_fails: Leaving stopwords in keyword queries causes high-frequency words to trigger millions of false positive matches.

name: Faceted Search Aggregations over Semi-Structured JSON Attributes
description: When a customer searches for 'laptops', e-commerce search engines return matching items along with dynamic facet counts (e.g. Brand: Apple (12), Dell (8); RAM: 16GB (15), 32GB (5)) extracted from JSON specs.
why_it_fails: Running separate queries for each facet dimension multiplies query latency and database load.

name: Financial Ledger Running Balance with Duplicate Timestamps
description: Tests window frame boundary specification (ROWS vs default RANGE) on duplicate timestamp ordering.
why_it_fails: In ANSI SQL and DuckDB, `SUM(...) OVER (ORDER BY col)` defaults to `RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` rather than `ROWS`. When two rows have identical ordering keys (same entry_time), RANGE treats them as equal peers and includes BOTH rows in the aggregate for the first row, prematurely applying the peer sum ($80.00 instead of $50.00). Strict cumulative calculations require explicit `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` and tie-breaker sorting.

name: Trigram / N-Gram Token Substring Matching for Technical Error Logs
description: In observability platforms (Datadog, Splunk), engineers search stack traces with partial error signatures. Trigram decomposition enables robust partial substring index matching.
why_it_fails: Full regex evaluations on raw million-line log tables trigger catastrophic backtracking.

name: Dynamic Query Synonym Expansion via Relational Thesaurus
description: When a customer searches for 'sofa', they also expect to see listings titled 'couch' or 'settee'. Expanding queries using a synonym thesaurus bridges terminology gaps.
why_it_fails: Hardcoding synonyms into client-side application code makes vocabulary updates inflexible.

name: Search Autocomplete Suggestion with Popularity Frequency Weighting
description: As users type 'air...', instant search suggests 'air fryer' (100k searches) before 'air mattress' (5k searches). Suggestions must match the prefix AND rank by historical popularity.
why_it_fails: Alphabetical sorting of prefix matches suggests obscure terms before popular items.

name: High-Precision Boolean Search with Negation and Grouping
description: Legal e-discovery and patent search rely on exact Boolean syntax: (patent AND battery) NOT (lithium OR phone). Negations must be strictly applied without dropping valid candidate documents.
why_it_fails: Poor operator precedence in SQL boolean expressions causes negated terms to drop unrelated valid results.

name: TF-IDF (Term Frequency - Inverse Document Frequency) in Pure SQL
description: TF-IDF is the foundational algorithm of information retrieval. Calculating it directly in SQL provides deep insight into term uniqueness across a corpus without requiring Python.
expected_columns: doc_id; term; term_count; tf; idf; tfidf_score
why_it_fails: Calculating document frequency across millions of documents requires careful window partitioning to avoid Cartesian explosions.

name: Discounted Cumulative Gain (DCG) with Search Position Bias Discount
description: Users are far more likely to click the #1 search result than the #5 result regardless of relevance. Ranking quality is measured via Discounted Cumulative Gain: DCG = SUM(relevance / log2(rank + 1)).
why_it_fails: Simple click counts reward poorly placed relevant items unfairly.

name: Alphanumeric SKU Matching with Punctuation & Case Invariance
description: Customers search for model numbers in messy formats: 'wh-1000xm5', 'WH1000-XM5', 'wh 1000 xm5'. Robust search normalizes punctuation and whitespace before matching.
why_it_fails: Exact string equality misses 90% of technical product searches due to hyphens and spaces.

name: Dynamic Negative Keyword Exclusion in E-Commerce Filters
description: A user searches 'monitor -curved' to find flat computer monitors. The engine must extract positive search terms and suppress any record containing the negative terms.
why_it_fails: Negative keywords must not exclude items where the negative term appears with negation qualifiers (e.g. 'not curved').

name: Multi-Lingual Catalog Routing by Detected ISO Language Code
description: Global portals store titles in multiple localized columns (title_en, title_es, title_fr). Queries are dynamically routed to the matching language column based on user locale.
why_it_fails: Searching across all language columns simultaneously creates false-positive matches due to inter-language false cognates.

name: Zero-Result Search Query Relaxation (Strict AND -> Loose OR Fallback)
description: If a multi-word search query (e.g. 'ergonomic mechanical wireless split keyboard') returns zero results under strict AND matching, modern engines gracefully relax to OR matching.
why_it_fails: Failing to return fallback results leads to user bounce and abandoned sessions.

name: Sequential Multi-Stage User Onboarding Conversion Funnel
description: Calculates user conversion through a multi-step sequence where events must strictly obey chronological order.
why_it_fails: Frontier models frequently calculate funnel conversions using independent conditional aggregations (COUNT DISTINCT CASE WHEN event = 'purchase'). This completely ignores the chronological order requirement (t_view < t_cart < t_purchase), mistakenly counting users who purchased via separate shortcuts or had events recorded out of sequence as successful sequential conversions.

name: Search Snippet Extraction: Context Window Around Matching Terms
description: Search results show a preview snippet containing the searched keyword with 30 characters of surrounding context rather than the beginning of a 2,000-word article.
why_it_fails: Substring extraction crashes when matching keywords appear near the very beginning or end of the text.

name: Customer Search-to-Purchase Path Attribution (Session Query Lift)
description: E-commerce search product managers need to know which search queries drove actual revenue. We link search queries to checkout events within the same 30-minute session.
expected_columns: order_id; user_id; order_total; attributing_search_query; searched_at; ordered_at
why_it_fails: Attributing purchases to search queries that occurred after the purchase order was placed.

name: Fuzzy Customer Entity Resolution across Disparate Data Sources
description: Merging CRM and billing databases requires linking customers with slight name and address variations (e.g. 'Robert Smith, 123 Main St' vs 'Bob Smith, 123 Main Street').
expected_columns: crm_id; crm_name; bill_id; billing_name; zip_code; name_similarity
why_it_fails: Pairwise fuzzy string matching over millions of records is computationally prohibitive without blocking/canopy clustering.

name: Search Term Co-Occurrence Matrix (Market Basket of Search Queries)
description: To suggest related searches, engines analyze queries searched together in the same session (e.g. users searching 'monitor' also search 'hdmi cable' 42% of the time).
why_it_fails: Self-joining search sessions without ordering (`a.term < b.term`) doubles matrix size with duplicate reversed pairs.

name: 'Did You Mean?' Query Spell-Correction Suggestion Engine
description: When a query produces few results, search engines recommend a spell-corrected candidate word from the catalog vocabulary that has the lowest edit distance and highest document frequency.
why_it_fails: Suggesting rare typos back to users rather than verified popular vocabulary terms.

name: Hybrid Search with Hard Categorical Filter & Soft Merchant Quality Boost
description: Top marketplaces enforce strict hard filters (in-stock, prime shipping) while soft-boosting items based on merchant review rating: final_score = text_relevance * (1.0 + 0.1 * merchant_rating).
why_it_fails: Hard-filtering by rating eliminates high-relevance new merchants with few reviews.

name: Hierarchical Bill of Materials (BOM) Cost Rollup via Recursive CTE
description: Manufacturing an electric vehicle requires thousands of nested parts (Car -> Battery Pack -> Cell Module -> Lithium Cathode). Calculating unit cost requires rolling up quantities across arbitrary depth levels.
why_it_fails: Fixed joins only support fixed depth hierarchies (e.g. 3 levels max). If an assembly has 6 levels, fixed joins miss the lowest-tier parts entirely.

name: Organizational Reporting Depth & Management Span of Control
description: HR analytics measures how deep the management chain is from the CEO to individual contributors and calculates direct vs indirect headcounts for each manager.
why_it_fails: Unbounded recursive queries crash if there is an accidental circular reporting loop (e.g. A reports to B, B reports to A).

name: Transitive Fraud Ring & Sybil Account Detection via Device Links
description: Financial fraudsters create hundreds of fake accounts linked by shared credit cards, device fingerprints, or IP addresses. Finding all accounts transitively connected to a confirmed fraudster exposes the syndicate.
why_it_fails: Looking only 1 hop away misses fraudsters who funnel funds through mule intermediary accounts.

name: Cycle Detection in Directed Dependency Graphs with Visited Array
description: In build systems (e.g. Webpack, Bazel) or task scheduling, circular dependencies (Task A -> Task B -> Task A) cause deadlocks. The engine must detect cycles and abort gracefully.
why_it_fails: Standard recursive CTEs without cycle tracking loop infinitely until the database crashes with out-of-memory errors.

name: Rolling 7-Day Window Aggregation without Quadratic Self-Joins
description: Tests whether models leverage native SQL range window frames over non-equi self-joins that cause quadratic memory and CPU explosions.
why_it_fails: Frontier models frequently generate triangular self-joins (JOIN ON b.date BETWEEN a.date - 6 AND a.date) instead of standard SQL RANGE window functions. On enterprise data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, DuckDB), this produces an O(N^2) join operator (such as PIECEWISE_MERGE_JOIN or nested-loop joins) that degrades from linear to quadratic complexity and risks memory spills or warehouse timeouts.

name: Lowest-Cost Routing across Logistics Hubs via Recursive Dijkstra
description: Supply chain networks ship containers through intermediary freight hubs. Finding the cheapest transit path from Source to Destination minimizes freight costs.
why_it_fails: Evaluating all combinations without cost bounding leads to exponential path explosion.

name: Causal Microservice Incident Root-Cause Dependency Chain
description: When a user checkout fails, it could be caused by payments, auth, database, or network. Tracing dependencies upwards from the affected user service identifies the underlying root-cause service failure.
why_it_fails: Diagnosing downstream symptoms rather than the root upstream failed dependency.

name: Graph Connected Components Labeling via Min-ID Propagation
description: Graph connected components partition isolated clusters of customers or machines. Propagating the minimum account ID across edges assigns every node in the same component a shared group ID.
why_it_fails: Standard SQL engines lack graph primitives, forcing expensive external graph database licenses.

name: Network Node In-Degree Centrality and Influence Ranking
description: Social network influence and API hub criticality are determined by node in-degree centrality (number of inbound links from distinct entities).
why_it_fails: Counting total edges without filtering distinct source nodes allows a single spammer to inflate influencer metrics.

name: Task Scheduling Critical Path Method (CPM) Duration Analysis
description: Project managers identify the 'Critical Path'—the longest sequence of dependent tasks that dictates the minimum project completion time.
why_it_fails: Adding task durations without considering parallel execution branches yields an unrealistically inflated project timeline.

name: Multi-Level Affiliate Referral Tree Commission Rollup (Tier 1-3)
description: Affiliate programs reward referrals up to 3 tiers deep (Direct referrer gets 10%, Tier 2 gets 5%, Tier 3 gets 2.5% of purchase amount).
why_it_fails: Hardcoded 3-way self-joins fail to handle users whose upline is only 1 or 2 tiers deep without complex coalesce logic.

name: Multi-Parent Shared Infrastructure Cost Allocation Rollup
description: Cloud infrastructure (e.g. shared Kubernetes cluster) is co-owned by multiple products with fractional split percentages. Costs must cascade down to consumer business units.
why_it_fails: Failing to multiply split percentages down the DAG results in allocated costs exceeding 100% of actual spend.

name: Triangular FX Currency Arbitrage Detection (Loop Profitability)
description: High-frequency FX trading bots scan for triangular arbitrage where converting USD -> EUR -> JPY -> USD yields more than 1.00 USD after exchange rates.
expected_columns: curr_start; curr_mid1; curr_mid2; curr_end; loop_multiplier; profit_margin_pct
why_it_fails: Missing currency conversion bid-ask spreads causes false positive arbitrage signals that lose money in practice.

name: Transactional State Machine Transition Sequence Verification
description: Financial compliance requires payment transactions to strictly follow the state sequence: INITIATED -> AUTHORIZED -> CAPTURED -> SETTLED. Any transaction skipping steps is flagged as fraudulent.
why_it_fails: Verifying status counts without checking transition sequence allows out-of-order state transitions.

name: Chasm Trap Resolution: Multi-Table 1:N Aggregation without Fan-Out Inflation
description: When an order has multiple discounts AND multiple shipment records, joining both child tables directly to the order creates a cross product that multiplies sales figures by 4x. Pre-aggregating each child table in CTEs before joining preserves financial integrity.
why_it_fails: Frontier models routinely join all tables before GROUP BY, causing catastrophic silent metric corruption.

name: SARGable Temporal Partition Pruning and Exact Boundary Range
description: Tests SARGable timestamp filtering and strict month boundary conditions, preventing full-scan string functions and end-of-interval leaks.
why_it_fails: Models frequently write `BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-02-01'`, which is inclusive on both ends and mistakenly captures records occurring exactly at midnight on February 1st (leaking records into the previous month's report). Alternatively, models wrap timestamp columns in non-SARGable scalar functions (like strftime or date_part), defeating column min/max partition pruning in columnar engines.

name: Three-Valued Logic Safe Anti-Join (Eliminating the NOT IN NULL Trap)
description: Marketing queries to find active customers who have not churned often use `WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM churned_users)`. If a single `NULL` exists in `churned_users`, SQL three-valued logic causes the entire query to return ZERO rows.
why_it_fails: In SQL, `val NOT IN (1, NULL)` evaluates to `UNKNOWN`, which evaluates to `FALSE` in WHERE clauses, silently discarding every single record.

name: Dynamic PIVOT of Monthly Revenue by Product Category
description: Financial reporting requires transforming normalized long-form transaction rows into cross-tabulated wide financial matrices (Months along the top, Categories down the side).
why_it_fails: Writing dozens of manual `CASE WHEN month = '2026-01' THEN amount ELSE 0 END` expressions is brittle and verbose.

name: Dynamic UNPIVOT of Wide Tabular Sensor / Survey Metrics
description: Legacy data or spreadsheet exports often arrive with metric names as column headers (cpu, memory, disk). Normalizing them into key-value pairs is necessary for time-series modeling.
why_it_fails: Chaining 10 UNION ALL queries multiplies read passes over the source data.

name: List Lambdas for High-Performance Nested Array Transformations
description: Modern analytical warehouses store nested array payloads (e.g. array of discount percentages). Transforming or filtering elements directly inside the array without unnesting and re-aggregating saves massive compute.
why_it_fails: Unnesting arrays to flat rows and re-aggregating with LIST() triggers expensive hash shuffles.

name: Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) Robust Statistical Outlier Detection
description: Traditional standard deviation Z-scores fail in the presence of extreme outliers because the outliers themselves distort the mean and standard deviation. MAD is a robust statistical scale estimator.
why_it_fails: Mean and standard deviation break down completely on fat-tailed or skewed data distributions.

name: Robust Z-Score Normalization using Median and Interquartile Range (IQR)
description: Standardizing skewed metrics (like API response latency) for machine learning feature pipelines requires scaling by IQR (Q3 - Q1) rather than standard deviation.
why_it_fails: Standard Z-score produces biased features when distributions have heavy tails.

name: Financial Ledger Running Total: ROWS vs. RANGE Semantic Contrast
description: In financial auditing, understanding the exact behavioral difference between `ROWS BETWEEN` and `RANGE BETWEEN` prevents duplicate-timestamp errors from failing regulatory ledger reconciliations.
why_it_fails: The ANSI SQL default for window frames with ORDER BY is `RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`, which aggregates identical peers together into one lump sum.

name: SARGable Partition Pruning: Exact Half-Open Date Boundary Ranges
description: When filtering analytical partitions for a calendar month, `BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-01-31'` leaks into February 1st if timestamps contain hours/minutes, while `strftime('%m', ts) = '01'` disables partition pruning entirely.
why_it_fails: Subtle boundary leakage or full table scans caused by non-SARGable WHERE predicates.

name: Window Peer Frame Exclusion: EXCLUDE GROUP for Clean Cross-Group Contrast
description: When comparing sales across product categories or dates, analysts want to compute the average of all other groups, strictly excluding the entire current group.
why_it_fails: Computing group baselines without excluding the current group dilutes contrast in small sample sizes.

name: Window Frame Ties Exclusion: EXCLUDE TIES for Unbiased Cumulative Totals
description: In financial ranking, when multiple entities have the exact same score, evaluating cumulative rank metrics without self-reinforcing duplicate ties prevents tied participants from skewing percentiles.
why_it_fails: Tied participants mutually inflate each other's cumulative metrics.

name: Market Basket Association Rules: Support, Confidence, and Lift in Pure SQL
description: Data miners discover product affinities ('Customers who buy Item A also buy Item B') using Support, Confidence, and Lift metrics computed directly from transaction tables.
expected_columns: item_a; item_b; pair_baskets; support; confidence; lift
why_it_fails: Generating cross-products across all transactions creates memory spills on large catalogs.

name: Kaplan-Meier Non-Parametric Customer Survival Analysis in SQL
description: Actuarial and SaaS subscription models estimate the probability of customer survival past Day T, accounting for right-censored users who haven't churned yet.
why_it_fails: Naively dividing churned users by total signups underestimates customer lifetime value.

name: Dynamic Equi-Depth Histogram Binning via NTILE in Pure SQL
description: Creating balanced feature histograms for ML requires equal-depth binning (each bucket contains an equal number of records) rather than equal-width binning.
why_it_fails: Equal-width bins leave high-value tail bins completely empty on skewed power-law distributions.

name: Rolling 7-Day Distinct Active Users without Triangular Join Explosion
description: Calculates rolling 7-day distinct active users per calendar day. SQL window functions forbid COUNT(DISTINCT) over range frames, causing frontier models to generate catastrophic O(N^2) triangular self-joins that blow up memory.
why_it_fails: Joining user_activity directly to itself on an inequality date range produces an O(N^2) Cartesian row explosion. For 1M rows, an unaggregated triangular join emits over 7M intermediate rows and triggers an IE_JOIN or Nested Loop join, overflowing RAM. The optimal pattern aggregates users into daily sets first before evaluating rolling intervals.

name: Dual-Constraint Sessionization: 30-min Inactivity AND 4-Hour Absolute Hard Cap
description: Groups web clickstream events into sessions. A new session starts if: 1) more than 30 minutes pass between consecutive events, OR 2) more than 4 hours have elapsed since the session genesis event.
why_it_fails: Frontier models only check the consecutive step lag (> 30 min). When an automated bot or persistent user emits events every 15 minutes continuously for 12 hours, the naive query leaves them in a single endless session, completely violating the 4-hour max session cap constraint.

name: Vector Nearest Neighbors: The Post-Filtering Empty Set Trap
description: Demonstrates the classic vector database failure mode where applying relational metadata filters AFTER Top-K vector retrieval discards valid results, returning an empty result set.
why_it_fails: Post-filtering vector retrieval (LIMIT 2 inside a subquery before WHERE filters) selects the globally highest similarity items (item 1 and item 2). Because item 1 is $150 (exceeds $50) and item 2 is 'clothing', the outer WHERE filter discards both, returning 0 rows! Relational filters must be applied as PRE-FILTERS.

name: ASOF Point-in-Time Quote Matching with 500ms Expiry Tolerance
description: Matches executed trades with the prevailing market quote as-of the trade timestamp, but enforces a strict 500ms staleness tolerance. Stale market data must not be matched.
why_it_fails: Standard ASOF joins without a staleness tolerance check blindly match trades to arbitrarily old quotes from hours or days ago. For Trade 1, naive SQL matches the 2-minute-old quote ($150.10) instead of returning NULL, resulting in stale execution data.

name: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) Hybrid Retrieval without Scale Collapse
description: Fuses BM25 keyword rankings and vector cosine similarity rankings using rank-based Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60), preventing unbounded BM25 scores from dominating vector scores.
why_it_fails: Frontier models frequently confuse RRF rank fusion with raw score addition (bm25_score + vector_sim). Because BM25 scores can reach 400+ while cosine similarity is bounded between 0 and 1, adding raw scores allows BM25 to completely drown out semantic vector relevance.

name: Directed Dependency Graph Cycle Protection via Visited Array Path
description: Traverses downstream dependencies in a directed acyclic graph that contains an intentional cyclic loop (A -> B -> C -> A), requiring visited path arrays to prevent infinite recursion OOM.
why_it_fails: Standard recursive CTEs without cycle tracking (omitting visited array state) enter an infinite recursion loop on cyclic graphs, causing DuckDB or any relational database to fail with a max-recursion limit error or crash with an Out-of-Memory exception.

name: Bitemporal Auditing: Retroactive Policy Revision Point-in-Time State
description: Reconstructs historical corporate insurance coverage on an effective business date, as known to the system on an audit date prior to a retroactive backdated modification.
why_it_fails: Frontier models ignore the second time dimension (system transaction time) and only filter on valid_from / valid_to. This incorrectly matches the retroactive modification ($500), which was not entered into the database until May 1st, failing regulatory compliance auditing.

name: Financial Ledger Running Total with Transaction Reversal Nullification
description: Calculates running account balance where REVERSAL records completely void specific prior transaction IDs, removing both the original transaction and the reversal record from net cumulative balance.
why_it_fails: Naive queries sum all records including reversed transactions. In our ledger, naive sum includes entry 2 (+$200) at step 2, temporarily inflating the running balance to $700 before entry 4 subtracts it. True ledger auditing requires excluding voided entries from the active sequence.

name: Exponential Half-Life Multi-Touch Marketing Attribution Normalized to 100%
description: Calculates exponential time-decay attribution across previous marketing touches (7-day half-life: w = 2^(-delta_t / 7)), strictly normalizing touchpoint weights so attributed revenue sums to exactly 100% of conversion value.
why_it_fails: Naive queries multiply raw exponential decay directly by order revenue without dividing by the sum of weights. In our scenario (raw weights sum to 1.75), naive attribution distributes 175% ($612.50) of the actual $350.00 revenue, severely corrupting marketing ROI calculations.

name: Association Rule Lift Matrix with Directional Pair Evaluation
description: Calculates market basket association rule Lift for directional product pairs (A -> B), correctly eliminating self-pairs and evaluating directional confidence.
why_it_fails: Naive models omit self-pair elimination (producing trivial rules like Bread -> Bread with 100% confidence), fail to normalize by total baskets, or confuse raw co-occurrence counts with statistical Lift.
